content: 1. GRAMMAR: Correct these errors: a) 'The data shows that temperatures is rising.' b) 'Pollution are destroying coral reefs.' c) 'According to WWF, dolphins uses sound to communicate.'

2. PUNCTUATION: Fix these sentences: a) 'Climate change is serious it affects everyone.' b) 'Scientists believe that the ocean is warming however they disagree on the rate.' c) 'The results show that 60% of dolphins showed signs of stress.'
3. MATH SPIRAL: Final data accuracy check. Write each statistic from your report, its source, and verify it is correct. Put ✓ for verified, ✗ for incorrect (then fix).

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Proofreading is the FINAL step before submitting any written work. It focuses on ACCURACY — catching grammar errors, spelling mistakes, punctuation problems, and formatting issues.
content: 📖 Proofreading is the FINAL step before submitting any written work. It focuses on ACCURACY — catching grammar errors, spelling mistakes, punctuation problems, and formatting issues.

Professional proofreaders use specific techniques: Read ALOUD — your ear catches errors your eye misses. Read BACKWARDS (sentence by sentence from the end) — this forces you to focus on each sentence individually. Use a CHECKLIST — systematically check one type of error at a time. CHECK CITATIONS — are all sources cited? Are citation formats consistent?

Common errors in student writing include: subject-verb agreement ('The data show' not 'The data shows'), tense consistency (stick to present tense for facts), apostrophes (it's = it is; its = belonging to it), comma splices (two sentences joined with only a comma — use a full stop or a connecting word).
After proofreading, your report is ready for its FINAL FORMAT — title page, headings, bibliography.
